children: The recent conflict between leading telcos Bharti Airtel, Reliance Jio, and Vodafone Idea (Vi) regarding mobile number portability tactics strongly indicates a change in market dynamics, moving away from the assumed duopoly, according to experts.

Leading telecom companies Airtel and Jio recently wrote to the sector watchdog, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), alleging that the third telecom service provider (TSP), Vi, attempted to poach users to its network by offering special plans and hindering the porting-out process by blocking SMS messages.

Sources familiar with the situation said that the call recordings shared in the matter may prove ineffective in terms of the claims. However, TRAI has stated that it will consider the grievances and has directed Vi to conduct an internal review accordingly.
More interesting than the allegations, experts following the development said the letter hints at an interesting change in the telco ecosystem.

“People believed that Vi is far too entangled in legal hassles. Now, it has gotten a breather and can pivot away from defensive tactics. Other companies know they can’t ignore Vi anymore,” said Faisal Kawoosa, Chief Analyst and Founder of Techarc.

When asked whether Vi has, in fact, flouted regulations by trying to onboard rival companies’ customers, Naqeeb Ahmed Kazia, Partner at CMS Induslaw, said, “MNP is designed to allow subscribers to switch between networks. As a result, chasing a competitor’s customer is permitted and not illegal.”

However, a telco is not permitted to offer differential pricing to subscribers if they were to port to its network. This means that if Vi is found in contravention of TRAI regulations, the regulator will order the withdrawal or modification of the contravening plans, direct the TSP to report all tariff plans to TRAI, and possibly impose a monetary penalty. According to Mahesh Uppal, Director of Comm First (India), the penalty would not be of major consequence.

However, a TRAI decision in 2021 prohibits blocking or delaying porting. At the time, TRAI stated that all telecom operators must allow customers to send and receive SMSes during porting procedures. Interestingly, this decision was also borne out of a complaint by Jio against Vi for removing SMS from its ₹99 base-level plan.

This means that a telco cannot refuse a valid port-out under the MNP regulations. If a subscriber is leaving, the telco must let them send the SMS to 1900 and issue the Unique Porting Code (UPC) without delay, on a non-discriminatory basis.

“So, if Vi is shown to have throttled or delayed the SMS or the UPC in some circles, that would prima facie breach these rules,” said Kazia, adding that TRAI could order corrective steps for the affected subscribers and impose a penalty on Vi.

title: Mobile number portability row hints at a shift in market dynamics, say experts
